overview: This table groups a character's battle voice lines so the game can pick lines for actions, reactions, and chosen voice styles, including low health.
description: Bundles the action-specific CharacterVoiceGroupDataTable IDs for one character voice variant (default/TypeA/TypeB/low-HP), selected by the active action or battle situation.

Id.simple: The name of this voice style, which the game picks from the player's voice setting or low health.
Id.technical: FName primary key. CharacterSoundDataTable.Id_CharacterVoiceGroupSet holds candidate IDs; AGameCharacter::FindCharacterVoiceGroupSetRow uses element 0 for mode 0, the saved NormalAttackVoiceIndex for mode 1, the saved CursedEnergyAttackVoiceIndex for mode 2, and element 3 for low-HP mode 3, then resolves the first row with this Id. Invalid indices or None yield no row. Export spells it ID.

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_DefaultAction.simple: Which voice lines play for general actions, even when the character's health is low.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_DefaultAction.technical: FName. Resolved by Action_FindCharacterVoiceGroupRow over DTM.CharacterVoiceGroupDataTables (+0x530) into a CharacterVoiceGroup row; None is rejected by the finder. Generic voice Kind 1 disables the low-HP set override and uses the request Index into that row's Id_VoiceGroup array.

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_NormalAttack1.simple: Which voice lines play on the first hit of a normal attack, including its automatic and airborne versions.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_NormalAttack1.technical: FName. Resolved by Action_FindCharacterVoiceGroupRow over DTM.CharacterVoiceGroupDataTables (+0x530) into a CharacterVoiceGroup row; the selected row supplies Id_VoiceGroup entries for the attack step. For Kind 2 the active action's virtual GetVoiceGroupRow selects this field (Index 0 is replaced by the action's attack voice index). NormalAttack_1, its Auto variant and the air first-hit classes resolve this field; some character overrides use it too.

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_NormalAttack1_1.simple: Which voice lines play on the follow-up to the first normal hit, including automatic and airborne versions.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_NormalAttack1_1.technical: FName. Resolved by Action_FindCharacterVoiceGroupRow over DTM.CharacterVoiceGroupDataTables (+0x530) into a CharacterVoiceGroup row; It is separate from NormalAttack1, allowing a different voice group on the second hit.. NormalAttack_1_1 and _1_1_Auto actions (ground and air), plus a CP_120 override, resolve this field.

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_NormalAttack2.simple: Which voice lines play on the second hit of a normal attack, on the ground or in the air.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_NormalAttack2.technical: FName. Resolved by Action_FindCharacterVoiceGroupRow over DTM.CharacterVoiceGroupDataTables (+0x530) into a CharacterVoiceGroup row; None IDs yield no group.. NormalAttack_2 / _2_Auto and air variants resolve this field; CP_110, CP_120 and CN_140 overrides also select it.

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_NormalAttack2_1.simple: Which voice lines play on the follow-up to the second normal hit, in ground or air combos.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_NormalAttack2_1.technical: FName. Resolved by Action_FindCharacterVoiceGroupRow over DTM.CharacterVoiceGroupDataTables (+0x530) into a CharacterVoiceGroup row; Chosen instead of NormalAttack2 for the follow-up step.. NormalAttack_2_1 / _2_1_Auto (ground and air) and CP_110/CP_120 overrides resolve this field.

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_NormalAttack3.simple: Which voice lines play on the third hit of a normal attack, on the ground or in the air.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_NormalAttack3.technical: FName. Resolved by Action_FindCharacterVoiceGroupRow over DTM.CharacterVoiceGroupDataTables (+0x530) into a CharacterVoiceGroup row; It feeds the same two-step CharacterVoiceGroup to VoiceGroup chain.. NormalAttack_3 / _3_Auto and air variants resolve this field; CP_110 and CP_120 overrides also use it.

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_NormalAttack3_1.simple: Which voice lines play on the follow-up to the third normal hit, in ground or air combos.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_NormalAttack3_1.technical: FName. Resolved by Action_FindCharacterVoiceGroupRow over DTM.CharacterVoiceGroupDataTables (+0x530) into a CharacterVoiceGroup row; It is the follow-up counterpart of NormalAttack3.. NormalAttack_3_1 / _3_1_Auto (ground and air) and CP_110/CP_120 overrides resolve this field.

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_CursedEnergyAttac.simple: Which voice lines play for the first Cursed Energy attack at level one, and when no higher level is set.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_CursedEnergyAttac.technical: FName. FGameCharacterAction_CursedEnergyAttack1Base starts with the _1 field for level 1 and other unmatched levels, switches to _2 or _3 when GetCursedEnergyLevel() is 2 or 3; the chosen ID is resolved with bCheckNone=true.

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_CursedEnergyAttac.simple: Which voice lines play for the first Cursed Energy attack when the character reaches Cursed Energy level two.
Which voice lines play for the first Cursed Energy attack when the character reaches Cursed Energy level three.
Which voice lines play for the second Cursed Energy attack at level one. One character also uses them for an extra attack.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_CursedEnergyAttac.technical: FName. FGameCharacterAction_CursedEnergyAttack2Base starts with the _1 field and switches to _2/_3 at levels 2/3; CP_230 ExtraAttack_1 also reads the _1 field.

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_CursedEnergyAttac.simple: Which voice lines play for the second Cursed Energy attack when the character reaches Cursed Energy level two.
Which voice lines play for the second Cursed Energy attack when the character reaches Cursed Energy level three.

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_SuperCursedEnergy.simple: Which voice lines play during a super Cursed Energy attack, whichever Cursed Energy level is active.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_SuperCursedEnergy.technical: FName. FGameCharacterAction_SuperCursedEnergyAttackBase::GetVoiceGroupRow resolves this single field without level switching, then the regular VoiceGroup index selection follows.

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_ExtraAttack1.simple: Which voice lines play for some characters' extra attacks. Other characters use different lines, and a few listed choices have no known effect.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_ExtraAttack1.technical: FName. Used by CP_020, CP_050, CP_070 and CN_230 ExtraAttack_1 overrides (CN_230 via a direct table walk). CP_230 ExtraAttack_1 instead reads CursedEnergyAttack2_1, so this field is not universal. 132/151 exported rows set it to None; eight non-None IDs in CP_250/CP_260/CN_122/CN_250 rows have no group row in the supplied export and no reconstructed C++ reader was found for those characters.

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_ExtraAttack2.simple: Which voice lines play for the second extra attack, but only on the few characters that have one.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_ExtraAttack2.technical: FName. Used by CP_020 and CP_050 ExtraAttack_2 overrides; only those overrides were observed reading it. None IDs resolve to no group.

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_Attack.simple: Which voice lines play for general attack calls when the character makes an attack.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_Attack.technical: FName. Generic voice Kind 3 requires Index>0, resolves this field and selects Id_VoiceGroup[Index-1].

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_SituationAttack.simple: Which voice lines play when an opponent is close or the battle situation calls for a special reaction.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_SituationAttack.technical: FName. Generic voice Kind 4 resolves this field and uses Id_VoiceGroup[Index]; Kind 2/3 requests can be rewritten to Kind 4 when a qualified secondary target, bSituationCheck and wait-time/distance conditions pass. Kind 4 is low-HP-checked only at Index==2.

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_System.simple: Which voice lines play for general battle announcements. Low health changes the voice style used for a few of them.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_System.technical: FName. Generic voice Kind 5 resolves this field and indexes Id_VoiceGroup by Index; its nominal set mode is 2, but the low-HP override can replace it with mode 3 at Index 2 or 5/6. The candidate array is read after mode selection.

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_Damage1.simple: Which voice lines play when the character takes ordinary damage.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_Damage1.technical: FName. Generic voice Kind 6 requires Index>0, resolves this field and uses Id_VoiceGroup[Index-1].

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_Down.simple: Which voice lines play when the character is knocked down.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_Down.technical: FName. Generic voice Kind 8 resolves this field and uses Id_VoiceGroup[Index].

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_Guard.simple: Which voice lines play when the character guards an attack.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_Guard.technical: FName. Generic voice Kind 9 resolves this field and uses Id_VoiceGroup[Index].

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_SpecialDamage.simple: Which voice lines play when the character takes special damage, separate from ordinary damage reactions.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_SpecialDamage.technical: FName. Generic voice Kind 7 requires Index>0, resolves this field and uses Id_VoiceGroup[Index-1]; it is distinct from Damage1.

Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_Unique.simple: Which voice lines play for character-specific moments. Many characters leave this without lines.
Id_CharacterVoiceGroup_Unique.technical: FName. Generic voice Kind 10 resolves this field and uses Id_VoiceGroup[Index]. Many exported rows leave it None.

notes: The DataTable is loaded through DataTableLoaders into DTM.CharacterVoiceGroupSetDataTables (+0x520). AGameCharacter::FindCharacterVoiceGroupSetRow(Mode) reads ActionController slot 90's candidate FNames (normally CharacterSoundDataTable.Id_CharacterVoiceGroupSet): mode 0 uses element 0, mode 1 the saved NormalAttackVoiceIndex, mode 2 the saved CursedEnergyAttackVoiceIndex, and mode 3 element 3 (usually a *_PINCH row in the export). Out-of-range indices and NAME_None return no row; the first matching table in the array wins. CP_051's action controller overrides slot 90 while CP_051_Passive is active, substituting CP_051_2/TYPEA_2/TYPEB_2/PINCH_2.

PlayVoice Kind 2 (attack actions) selects a field through the active action's virtual GetVoiceGroupRow(VoiceSet), not through a fixed Kind-to-member mapping: normal attacks select NormalAttack*, cursed-energy/super attacks select level-specific fields, CP_020/CP_050/CN_230 extra attacks select their own fields, and CP_230 inlines its own finder. Its set mode comes from the action (normal attacks 1; cursed-energy/super and CP_020/CP_050 extra attacks 2; CP_070 extra attack 1). When request Index is 0 the action's GetAttackVoiceIndex() value is used; the resulting Id_VoiceGroup index has no bounds check and the group finder is called with bCheckNone=false.

For PlayVoice Kinds 1-10 the set row can be forced to mode 3 when HP/maxHP <= 0.3 (or maxHP <= 0), except Kind 1 explicitly disables that check; Kind 4 applies it only at Index==2 and Kind 5 only at Index 2/5/6. Mode 3 selects candidate element 3, not a field of the set row.

All 25 row members are reflected FName with no C++ initializer; the inline empty constructor (header line 86) leaves NAME_None. The export serializes all 25 columns on every row and uses 'None' for unused voice slots (no missing columns or non-None declared defaults).

Every non-None FName is a join to CharacterVoiceGroupDataTable (DTM +0x530), not directly to VoiceGroupDataTable. Action_FindCharacterVoiceGroupRow returns the first matching row and rejects NAME_None when bCheckNone=true; the observed C++ reads of these columns pass true or (in CP_230) check IsNone() explicitly. The selected CharacterVoiceGroup.Id_VoiceGroup[step] then joins to VoiceGroupDataTable, whose Id_Voice entries join to VoiceDataTable.

Indexing differs by generic Kind: Kinds 1/4/5/8/9/10 use Id_VoiceGroup[Index] directly; Kinds 3/6/7 require Index>0 and use Id_VoiceGroup[Index-1]; Kind 2 uses the attack voice index when Index==0. These are array indices, not IDs or counts, and no bounds check is performed at the read site.

The export has 151 unique rows (every row key equals its ID and there are no repeated keys). 147 are referenced by the 56 four-element CharacterSoundDataTable candidate arrays (12 slots are None); the remaining four are the CP_051 passive-only rows above. Many slots are None (for example 132/151 ExtraAttack1, 146/151 ExtraAttack2 and 97/151 Unique).

In the supplied export, eight non-None ExtraAttack1 IDs (CP_250, CP_260, CN_122, CN_250 base and PINCH rows) have no CharacterVoiceGroupDataTable row, and ten CharacterVoiceGroup.Id_VoiceGroup references in downstream rows have no VoiceGroupDataTable row; no reconstructed C++ reader for ExtraAttack1 in those four characters was found, so the reason is unresolved. C++ consumer evidence here comes from current Reconstruction sources with inline retail RVA annotations; retail Blueprint graphs were not reviewed, so Blueprint-only consumers cannot be excluded.

usages.detail: Selects a set row by saved voice variant or low-HP mode.
Normal-attack classes pick normal-attack fields from the set.
Cursed-energy classes pick level-specific fields from the set.
Kind 2 takes the set mode from the active attack action and is still subject to the low-HP mode override.
Shared group finder rejects None and returns the first matching CharacterVoiceGroup row.
Generic PlayVoice maps Kind to a set field, applies the Index convention, and indexes the resulting CharacterVoiceGroup row.
Character-specific extra-attack overrides pick their own fields.
CP_230 extra attack uses the CursedEnergyAttack2_1 field.
CP_051 passive buff replaces slot-90 candidate IDs with the four CP_051_*_2 set rows.
